# 03 — Your real alternative

What actually happens if this dies. **This single line decides whether you can run lion or are
stuck running fox**, whatever mode you would prefer.

A strong alternative is not confidence, it is arithmetic. "I publish it myself this afternoon" is
strong. "I keep looking" is weak. Write the true one — a play built on a walk-away you do not
have is the bluff that costs more than the deal was worth, and you only find out afterwards.

---

## If the deal in front of you dies

> [Concretely. What do you do instead, this week, and what does it cost you?]

## How easily they replace you

Honest answer, because it drives everything.

> [Are there twenty people who do what you do, or three? If twenty, what makes you the one they
> came to? That reason IS your leverage, and if you cannot name it, you do not have much.]

## What is NOT in this file, deliberately

**What a particular counterparty has already spent** — their meetings, their brief, their launch
date, whether they have told their boss. That belongs to ONE deal and changes with every thread,
so the skill reads it off the conversation each time (Step 1) rather than storing it here.

It matters, and it is the reason: it is the row that pushes a situation towards lion. A profile
that carried deal A's sunk costs would score deal B as though its counterparty were equally
committed, and the advice would come back harder than the facts support. This file is for what is
true about YOU across every deal.

## Your recurring counterparty types, with a standing read

One line each for the kinds of people you actually deal with. This is where the file earns
itself, because a standing read stops every situation starting from zero.

**[Inbound enquiries]** — Standing read: [what is usually really going on]

**[Agencies / intermediaries]** — Standing read: [e.g. the agency's margin is not your problem,
and the client usually does not know the agency is grinding]

**[Clients / retained work]** — Standing read: [e.g. scope drifts silently and gets absorbed.
Price the change when it appears, not at the end]

**[Partners / platforms]** — Standing read: [e.g. they want access to your audience for their
launch. That is a bigger ask than they frame it as]

**[Collaborators / swaps]** — Standing read: [e.g. audience sizes are rarely symmetrical and
nobody says so out loud. Check the ratio before agreeing an even split of effort]

**[Your own team]** — Not a counterparty. That is management, never a play.

## Timing

> [When should a hard message actually go out? One sent late at night costs you sleep for no
> gain, and one sent on a Friday sits unanswered all weekend.]
